thread:
sara: ACME prod webhooks started failing around 07:10 UTC, customer reports 403s from their firewall. They say our egress IP changed and their allowlist no longer matches.
acme-infra (via email): 'We only allow three IPs for inbound webhooks; we saw a new source IP at 07:08 and blocked it.'
nate: I checked egress metrics — NAT pool rebalanced in us-east-1 during autoscale at 07:07–07:09. SNAT IPs rotated between AZs. Likely root cause.
oscar: Any mTLS/TLS error logs on our side? I don't see client cert failures, just upstream 403s from the customer's firewall.
lena: Customer confirmed they use IP-based allowlist (not hostname). They also have strict host->ip mapping in firewall cache.
sara: Customer repro snippet they ran:
```
curl -v https://hooks.acme-prod.com/endpoint -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"evt":"ping"}'
# -> TLS handshake ok, then firewall returns 403/reset
```
nate: Quick check from one of our egress hosts:
```
$ sudo tcpdump -n host 3.44.55.123 and port 443 -c 5
# shows SYN from 3.44.55.123 -> 198.51.100.10
```
chris: 3.44.55.123 was not in their allowlist (they had 198.51.100.11/32 allowed). So when our SNAT used 3.44.55.123, it was blocked.
sara: Customer also mentioned their firewall caches the resolved IP for hooks.acme-prod.com for 30m and maps host->ip strictly. That cache contains the old SNAT-to-IP mapping.
oscar: Root cause summary: autoscale-triggered NAT rebound caused ephemeral SNAT addresses to change. Customer expects stable source IPs.
lena: Short-term workarounds: ask customer to add the full known pool range OR add the 3 sample IPs we saw and clear their firewall cache. Also recommend allowlisting by hostname + TLS client cert where possible.
sara: I sent customer an immediate list of three candidate IPs to add: 3.44.55.120, 3.44.55.121, 3.44.55.123 and asked them to clear firewall cache. Also opened INC-4721 for tracking.
nate: Customer requested proof those IPs belong to our egress pool. We'll provide an attestation including ASN and ROA: AS54123, + `whois` output and BGP origin.
oscar: Ops follow-up: file NET-1284 to add a GA option for reservable static egress IPs for Private customers. Prioritizing if customer chooses to buy the feature.
sara: Action items: (1) customer to add pool & flush firewall cache, (2) netops to prepare signed IP attestation, (3) product to estimate NET-1284 effort.
deploy-bot: incident created -> INC-4721 assigned to nate, oscar
lena: Marking P1 for support. Sara can you confirm when customer updates allowlist?
sara: Customer updated allowlist at 08:03 UTC — partial recovery: ~80% successful deliveries, still seeing intermittent 403s (likely TTL cache). I asked them to force-clear cache and re-run tests.
sara: Update 08:41 UTC — customer flushed cache and reports all webhooks are green. No more 403s.
chris: Recommend we proactively notify other Private/VPC customers about autoscale SNAT rotation behavior and suggested allowlist patterns.
oscar: Agree — I'll draft an advisory with recommended allowlist ranges, steps to request static egress, and BGP/ASN attestation snippets. Filed NET-1284 to track permanent option.
sara: Linking INC-4721 and NET-1284 for postmortem. Closing this thread unless we see regression.
